summary:
# NOTES: *The Indiscretions of a Lady's Maid* (William Le Queux, 1912, Eveleigh Nash)

**Frame:** Narrator Mariette Le Bas, 24, femme-de-chambre, dau. of Jacques Le Bas, peasant-proprietor of Pont-Pagny near Auxerre, Yonne. Speaks French, Italian, English, a little German. Wants £48/yr. Diary-style chapters, each headed by a date. Mixes French phrases. Ends by returning to Pont-Pagny with savings. Single book, 15 chapters.

## Ch I. Madame's Gentleman Friend (10 Apr)
- New post (17th in 5 yrs): Mrs. **Lucy Engleheart**, Cleveland Square, London. Husband **Monsieur Engleheart** (~30, City business, tall, clean-shaven). Overheard in Italian: "Benissimo! ... keep a still tongue?"
- Butler **Francis** (bald, dyed moustache, 8 yrs with master, prying, "keep a still tongue"; alias "Mr. Jennings"). Head housemaid **Griffiths** writes letters. Registry: Mrs. Banks.
- Madame's wedding ring left in dressing-table drawer.
- Monte Carlo, Hôtel de Paris. Madame sends Mariette to Nice. Lover: **Oswald B. Ogden**, pale American, inherited ~£5m (father cornered leather). Yellow motor. Stays at Hôtel Royal, Nice.
- Mariette follows Engleheart and Francis (as "Monsieur Vernon", straw hat) on Promenade des Anglais.
- Keyhole: Engleheart: "Francis is determined." Madame: "Mariette is a treasure... pretty, so may be useful." Francis advised paying Mariette 500 francs to go.
- Note to Ogden; he demands meeting at Casino terrace, 11pm. Madame wrecks room in rage.
- Daily Mail: Ogden engaged to **Gloria Dominick**, dau. of Charles H. Dominick, President, Philadelphia Railway.
- Back in London: writs at door; Mrs. Cooper a friend; Madame lost £1,000 at tables.
- Ogden loiters outside house with fair-haired friend. Demands Mariette not mention him.
- Study confrontation: Engleheart demands £5,000 for letters, to send to Miss Dominick. Ogden refuses; reveals he knew the scheme (a friend recognised Engleheart); demands £500 by noon next day or police. Calls Francis "clever old blackguard."
- Mariette leaves with trunk. Couple vanish overnight, debts in Bayswater.

## Ch II. The Wardrobe Drawer (9 Oct)
- **Branksome Court**, Bournemouth. **Lady Allardyce** (stout, blonde, "chic"); **Sir Hubert Allardyce** (ex-Minister in South America; short, stout, monocle, churchwarden). Footman **Henry**. Pekinese.
- Lady gives Mariette clothes from a wardrobe drawer; "I only like pretty girls."
- Mystery: Lady's secret meetings. Old woman at Pier gives message from "Mr. Charles"; mauve bag signal.
- **Charlie Shaw** (alias **George Gamlen**), Invalids' Walk; half-louis; later pressed for midnight meeting. Lady says Charles is her "very great friend", asks Mariette to be cover lover.
- Locked drawer (key left in): false bottom holds jewels, plated revolver, steel tools, black velvet loup. Mariette wears a diamond necklet in mirror.
- Lady overheard: "You married me for my money."
- Arcade: Charles gives brown-paper packet. Midnight conservatory visit. Two men with bull's-eye lantern (police). Charles arrested for theft of jewellery of **Baronne Veuillot** at Versailles. Lady tells Mariette to claim she was his lover.
- Papers: Bow Street report. Allardyces leave for India and Japan. Mariette dismissed (with present).
- Lady reveals: "Charles is my son." Charles transported to Devil's Island 3 months later.

## Ch III. Little Mrs. Otway (23 June)
- Mrs. **Lucy Otway** (~30, daughter of a grocer, Lower Sydenham). Grosvenor Street, Park Lane end. Husband **Jack/"Monsieur" Otway**, tall thin, owns major daily newspaper, millionaire at 40, seeking baronetcy. Butler **Joseph**, footman **Hinkson**. Wednesday entertainments.
- Letter from financier **Isaac Blumfeld** (Park Lane, white mansion, glass verandah) found in motor-coat; Mariette burns it.
- Rival: **Honourable Frank Carew** (Foreign Office, Carlos Place rooms). Bridge at **Lady Staverton**'s, Mount Street.
- Mariette spies for Madame outside Blumfeld's; sees Carew enter ~6pm. Blumfeld found shot in library ~11pm. Monsieur Otway: "Carr, the news-editor" rang.
- Carew asks Mariette to give alibi (5:30–7 at his rooms). Mariette refuses handshake.
- Carew: "Lunch at the Berkeley." Coroner: "Wilful murder against some person unknown."
- Otway library confession: Lucy went to Blumfeld, struggle with her husband's revolver, shot him. Carew sold secret treaty copy and correspondence (subsidies from foreign power to journal). Mariette paid £100, dismissed.

## Ch IV. The Noah's Ark (16 Feb)
- Mrs. **Ashley-Bond** (~30, cinnamon gown), Savoy Hotel. Husband in Germany. Companion **Madame Courtenay** (dark, Hebrew type); husband **Monsieur Courtenay** (short, podgy, turned-up moustache). Also "Monsieur" **Ashley-Bond** (~40, military, fair moustache). Bill from Shepherd's, Cairo.
- Sudden flight: Mariette sent via Harwich to Basle, Milan (Hôtel de Milan). Monsieur becomes **Captain Hugh Atherton**; Madame **Lady Hylda Atherton**, dau. of Earl of Ilfracombe.
- Milan: Biffi's café, Galleria; Bocconi's; Métropole (Madame Courtenay).
- Mariette accosted by **Pégard** (fake Lyons silk-traveller, actually sûreté), staged pickpocket at Milan cathedral.
- Flight: Rome plan, then Florence, Rimini (Aquila Nero), Brindisi, Reggio, Messina, **Villa Igiea**, Palermo. Kit-bag full of banknotes. Banks: Banca d'Italia, Banca Commerciale (Via Materassi), Quattro Canti, Bank of Sicily. Dance at Prefecture; turquoise Doeuillet gown.
- Naples steamer; parcel is child's **Noah's Ark** (tin, vermilion roof, white sides, one black window). Naples → Genoa, Hôtel de Londres, Piazza Corvetto, meets Courtenay as Italian workman; under Annunziata portico.
- Marseilles, Hôtel Louvre et Paix: Mariette arrested. Courtenay caught at Modane with 170,000 francs in Ark; sentenced by Assize Court of the Seine to 15 years forced labour.
- Forgery of £10 Bank of England notes; Hounslow house. Ashley-Bonds never seen again.

## Ch V. Guilty Bonds (29 July)
- Registry-office criticism. Eight situations in three months; 3% fee.
- **Hembury Court**, near Totnes, Devonshire. **Monsieur Philip Alleyne** (~40, stout, round face, library reclining, whisky) and **Madame Ethel Alleyne** (~28, tall, thin, blue eyes, morphia, hunts). Chauffeur **Chapman** (honest; also "Jack"). Half share in Plymouth factory.
- Alleyne tries to kiss Mariette; threatens Madame with revolver; "Reids' governess."
- Madame's lover **Major Hubert Ward** (tall, dark, Tyrolese hat), guest at Cullaford Hall (Colliers).
- Diamond tiara (wheat-ears, gift from father). Plymouth telephone call.
- Midnight: Madame and visitor in palm-court; her neck scratched; diamond necklet, bracelet, ruby-emerald butterfly stolen. Mariette sees man in dark overcoat and golf-cap.
- Shot in wood at night. Jewel-safe key concealed in Mariette's trunk.
- Telegram; Madame goes to London (Carlton). Ward demands £2,000; Madame's bigamy; Ward once shot a man named **Ducane**; Williamson (accomplice, shot by Alleyne in Johannesburg).
- Night: Ward steals Alleyne's bonds, safe-alarm rings; Alleyne shoots Ward. Ward's dying words: "Forgive!... Ethel, my wife."
- Madame's history: married Ward at 18 at Cape; he's a card-sharper. Alleynes move to Florence after stock losses.

## Ch VI. The Mystery of Monsieur (15 Jan)
- Stamford, Lincolnshire, opposite the "George". Mr. and Mrs. **Ralph and Lucy Henniker** (Mrs. ~26, giddy, fair). Butler **Gray** (clean-shaven, high cheekbones, grey hair). Three raw maids.
- French waiter at the George, **Jean Valensi** (secret police agent). Warns of mystery.
- Stained blood on Madame's blue chiffon sleeve; she hides it.
- Telegram from Abbeville: "All well. Bring Mariette to Hôtel Continental, Paris. Start to-night.—RALPH."
- Gray discharged (fake); overheard plan to get rid of Mariette.
- Paris: flat above a hat-shop, Rue Lafayette. Madame counts foreign bonds, hides under mattress.
- Ralph arrives, unshaven; Gray watches from doorway opposite.
- Madame poisons Mariette's coffee; Mariette collapses.
- Found by Jean (agent) and **Inspector Allen** (Met). **Norfolk Square murder**: **George Bicknell** knifed/drugged; safe emptied.
- Ralph Henniker (alias Farmer, Mortimer) shot himself in private hotel near Madeleine. Madame sentenced to 20 years penal servitude. Gray jailed at Marseilles for blackmail.

## Ch VII. The Chamber of Secrets (2 July)
- Florence, 18 April 1909. Prefecture (old Medici palace). **Chevalier Luigi Ansaldi** (tall, thin, bald, dark beard, chief of secret police).
- Mariette's mistress **Madame Kennedy-Foster** (widow; Villa Luba, Viale; devout Catholic). Her mysterious "friend" **William Cornforth** (tall, thin, Villa Borelli; murdered).
- Caretaker **Enrico Ferri** (Villa Pontedera) reports old woman visits at 3am on Jan 2, 11, 16, 26.
- Ansaldi receives London warrant. Cornforth gone; old woman was seen leaving.
- Strong-room door: steel, bolted inside, combination lock. Opened by electric current. Inside: Cornforth shot in back, seated at desk, singed jacket, no weapon.
- Fussy Jewish police doctor (gold pince-nez): murder, not suicide.
- Scotland Yard telegram from **Chetwynd** (Commissioner): "Make no further inquiry... prevent Press from publishing."
- Mariette's Via Cavour pension.

## Ch VIII. What Was in the Strong Room (28 July)
- Hidden panel behind picture: unset gems (diamonds, rubies, emeralds), ruby ~50,000 francs. Valued later at £50,000 by **Cravanzola** (Rome jeweller). Held at Consul **Walker**'s request.
- Italian King wishes case hushed.
- **Carlo Bruno** (police agent, Merli his comrade) found shot dead in strong-room. Same wound.
- Cornforth had lived at Brunswick Square, Hove (Brighton).
- Mariette to London: meets **Chief-Inspector Stephens**, **Monsieur de Champfleur**, sister **Jeanne**. Stephens: Home Office wanted Cornforth arrested; "criminal by instinct."

## Ch IX. Concerns Two Visitors (2 Sept)
- Mariette in lodgings off King's Road, Chelsea.
- Visitors: **Karl Flugel** (old German, blue reefer, white spats, gold-rimmed glasses, fair beard) and **Agnes Cornforth** (fair, blue eyes, black dress, school-teacher near York).
- Flugel: "I know the truth." Wants money from Scotland Yard.
- Agnes believed drowned 18 months earlier (Sheringham; body washed up at Hunstanton).
- Agnes asks Mariette to keep her secret.

## Ch X. Contains Revelations (22 Dec)
- Mariette in Fiesole with **Frau Staben**. Summoned to Prefecture: arrest of Agnes at Villa Borelli. Flugel found shot dead there.
- Agnes reveals: Cornforth = **Electric ray inventor**; Hertzian rays concentrated. Mother = Mrs. Kennedy-Foster (Cornforth's wife), who visited disguised as old woman.
- Hidden battery bank; glass tubes broken; apparatus destroyed. Death rays from unswitched current.
- Agnes to Brussels with mother. Mariette gives notice.

## Ch XI. A Queer Ménage (6 Sept)
- Albert Hall Mansions, Kensington Gore. **Madame Shorland** (short, stout, fair, snub nose, "porky" face) and **Monsieur Shorland** (tall, bony, black hair, morose).
- Madame's night trips: Oakleigh Park, Whetstone, house "Allandale". Invalid **Mr. March** (Madame's father; receiver of stolen jewels; ~60; pale; spine trouble). Pearls from Chinese ginger-jar.
- **Lindermann** millionaires (John R. and **Ida**), Pittsburg; Rumpelmeyer's tea; Ritz. Ida's mother arrives ill ("Athenée").
- Château de Bouligny, Marlotte, Fontainebleau; agent **Lamb**. Lindermann speaks French secretly with a man.
- Marie Antoinette emerald crucifix worn by Ida. Louvre theft.
- **Inspector Jacques Lesage** (Paris Prefecture). Madame posted crucifix at Marlotte.
- Shorlands fled; Lindermanns vanish. Mariette paid off by Mr. March.

## Ch XII. A Peer of the Realm (5 Apr)
- **Lady Lydgate** ("Angel"; 26; dau. of Countess of Hannaford; sister married a duke). Husband **Earl of Lydgate** ("Tubby", Hubert). Lydgate Hall, Shropshire, sold to **Silas B. Shaw** of Chicago. House: South Street, Park Lane.
- Butler **Thompson** (48 yrs; hates Lady; "I could strangle her"). Children: Lord Staverton, Lady Enid (with Lady Middlecoombe).
- **Captain Fletcher** (York regiment). Lady dines alone in blue serge.
- 1 October: Earl shot at Berkshire pheasant shoot; Harley Street surgeon. Lady missing.
- Her farewell note; she eloped to Paris with Fletcher. Earl dies. Thompson's "my poor boy."

## Ch XIII. Concerning Madame's Luggage (29 Aug)
- **Madame Houget** (Provençal) and **Pierre Houget** (Lyons manufacturer, Hebrew type, jewellery). Gloucester Terrace.
- **Princess di Lastra a Signa** (moustache; daughters **Claudia** and **Vittorina**). Antique jewel collection; Sultan Suleyman's two sapphires (Princess wears as earrings).
- Trip to Vallombrosa. Victoria → Dover → Paris → Modane → Turin → Genoa → Pisa.
- Madame registers trunks only to Pisa. Feigns illness at Pisa; Claudia left with her; train to Florence at 5.40.
- Jewels hidden in trunk. **Jean Regnier** (baggage-porter, Paris–Modane express) with skeleton keys. Madame's plan: to Genoa, German liner, Bremen, Amsterdam (**Jacobsen**).
- Madame gives Mariette 1,000 francs.

## Ch XIV. Madame and the Butler (17 Feb)
- **Mrs. Wentworth** (tall, fair), Elmhurst Court, Sussex. **Captain Wentworth** (short, thick-set, ferret-eyed). Daughter **Doris** (10). Governess **Miss Wylde**. Butler **Ford** (Charles Ford, grey, side whiskers).
- Red double puncture marks (like snake-bite); later a third. Diphtheria, then typhoid.
- Previous governess **Lucie Perrin**; ring in birthday cake; **Alfred Ackland** (young suitor).
- Insurance ~£30,000.
- Dr. **Emmott** (Cavendish Square). Ford's "brother Gervais" in Earl's Court Road (bacteriologist).
- Ice pudding: Mariette denounces Ford: "Charles Ford, stand there! I accuse you!" Gelatin cultures on plate.
- Ford killed Perrin in illicit Hamburg gaming house; Madame co-owner.
- Madame: "They mean to kill me." Ford dismissed by Madame's threat.
- Mariette paid £100.

## Ch XV. The People at Lancaster Gate (11 June)
- Miss **Violet Rutherford-Morgan** (22, dark, chic). Father Rutherford-Morgan (round, gold glasses, broken arm in sling). Chauffeur **Edwards**.
- Monsieur uses the "broken" arm; Brighton, Métropole; writes letter.
- Cave (Ebury St, 44a; young blagueur).
- Solicitor **Percival** (really a detective).
- Horton Brothers, Old Bond Street (diamond merchants). Necklet worth £2,000; price agreed £1,680 (letter to "Henry Horton"; envelope switched to George Horton).
- Mariette arrested, taken to Vine Street. Real names: **Dick Traill** and **Lily Mayhew** (Shorland gang).
- Mariette returns to Pont-Pagny with savings, "shall not again go back to service."
